title: The Dynamic Earth: Plates, Quakes, Volcanoes, and Landscapes
summary: Twenty-seven standalone, evidence-led lectures following plate motion and earthquake physics through mountain building and geological time to ground failure, mineral resources, geothermal systems and field inference.
assumed_background: Basic familiarity with the Earth as a rocky planet. No prior course or advanced mathematics required.

lectures.title: The Ocean Floor Gave Earth Away: How Plate Tectonics Became Testable
lectures.description: Reconstructs plate tectonics from ocean-floor age, symmetrical magnetic reversal bands, earthquake belts and modern GNSS motion, distinguishing plates from continents.

lectures.title: The Planet We Cannot Open: How Seismic Waves Reveal the Interior
lectures.description: Derives the layered solid mantle, liquid outer core and solid inner core from body-wave paths, shadow zones, mechanical rheology and complementary gravity data.

lectures.title: The Engine Is Not a Conveyor Belt: Why Tectonic Plates Move
lectures.description: Teaches slab pull, ridge gravitational potential, mantle coupling, viscous resistance and the limits of textbook convection-belt cartoons.

lectures.title: The Ridge Is a Factory: Building Ocean Floor and Sliding Along Its Seams
lectures.description: Explains partial melting by decompression, newly formed oceanic crust, cooling and depth, active transforms versus inactive fracture zones and hydrothermal alteration.

lectures.title: Where the Ocean Floor Goes: Subduction, Arcs, and Colliding Continents
lectures.description: Connects slab bending, Wadati–Benioff seismicity, fluid-assisted mantle-wedge melting, megathrust rupture, tsunamis and continental collisions.

lectures.title: Why a Fault Lets Go: Elastic Strain, Friction, and Earthquake Rupture
lectures.description: Builds the elastic rebound model, fault types, effective stress and friction, propagating rupture, seismic moment, magnitude scaling and limits of earthquake prediction.

lectures.title: Listening to the Rupture: Seismic Waves, Shaking, and Tsunamis
lectures.description: Reads P- and S-wave arrival times, hypocenters, focal mechanisms, magnitude versus local shaking, basin effects, tsunamis and early-warning limits.

lectures.title: How Rock Becomes Magma: Melting Without an Underground Ocean
lectures.description: Separates decompression, volatile-assisted, and thermal melting from later crystallization, contamination, gas exsolution and magma ascent.

lectures.title: Why Volcanoes Behave Differently: Lava, Ash, and the Anatomy of an Eruption
lectures.description: Distinguishes lava, ash, pyroclastic currents and lahars through volatile exsolution, viscosity, source geometry and documented Mount St. Helens and Iceland cases.

lectures.title: Why Mountains Have Roots: Collision, Crustal Thickening, and Isostasy
lectures.description: Builds Airy-style crustal compensation from densities, then explains collision thrusts, flexure, erosion rebound and independent evidence for mountain roots.

lectures.title: The Rock Records Its Burial: Metamorphism, Pressure, and Exhumation
lectures.description: Develops metamorphic mineral stability and fabrics as distinct evidence, then reads burial, overprinting, subduction, exhumation and mineral dates as a path.

lectures.title: Rain Dissolves a Mountain: Weathering, Soils, and the Long Carbon Cycle
lectures.description: Contrasts mechanical and chemical weathering, derives silicate versus carbonate carbon accounting and explains why sediment, solute and climate feedback timescales differ.

lectures.title: Rivers Carry Mountains Away: Slopes, Sediment, and the Work of Water
lectures.description: Tracks sediment from hillslopes through channels into basins, teaching stream power, storage budgets, bedload, incision, base level and downstream effects of trapping sediment.

lectures.title: The Ice Was Moving: Glaciers, Valley Carving, and the Rebounding Earth
lectures.description: Explains why moving ice can have a retreating terminus, the physical origins of glacial landforms and sediments, and the land-motion component of relative sea level.

lectures.title: Where the Sediment Waits: Basins, Layers, and Buried Landscapes
lectures.description: Explains accommodation and subsidence, interprets depositional facies and missing time, and tests inferences from stratigraphic trends and sediment provenance.

lectures.title: A Cliff Is an Order of Events: Relative Time, Faults, and Missing Chapters
lectures.description: Uses a worked cross-cutting puzzle and Hutton’s Siccar Point unconformity to explain superposition, structural restoration, map inference and relative chronology.

lectures.title: Clocks Hidden in Crystals: Radioactive Dates and Geological Time
lectures.description: Explains parent–daughter decay, U–Pb zircon, argon cooling, closure temperature, detrital provenance and why a dated mineral records a specific event.

lectures.title: Reconstructing the Appalachians: A Mountain Range with Several Histories
lectures.description: Integrates collision chronology, thrust mapping, metamorphic conditions, sediment provenance, rock clocks and Mesozoic rifting into an evidence-based Appalachian reconstruction.

lectures.title: How a Hillside Holds Together: Friction, Water, and Sudden Failure
lectures.description: Builds shear-strength and pore-pressure mechanics, contrasts rockfall, rotational sliding and deep creep, and investigates the 2014 Oso landslide.

lectures.title: When the Valley Starts to Flow: Debris Flows, Fire, and Lahars
lectures.description: Explains dense sediment-water flow mechanics, postfire runoff, lahars, debris-flow runout and the 2018 Montecito event.

lectures.title: When the Ground Loses Its Strength: Liquefaction and Earthquake Ground Failure
lectures.description: Derives liquefaction from effective-stress loss, then distinguishes settlement, lateral spreading, shaking amplification and site investigation.

lectures.title: A Hazard Map Is a Question: Probability, Exposure, and Geological Risk
lectures.description: Distinguishes inventories, susceptibility, conditional probability, runout, exposure and risk, including the compounding of annual probabilities.

lectures.title: Why a Deposit Becomes Ore: How Geology Concentrates the Elements
lectures.description: Compares magmatic, hydrothermal, sedimentary, placer and weathering enrichment, and separates contained metal from recoverable ore.

lectures.title: When Hot Water Carries Metals: Hydrothermal Veins, Copper, and the Seafloor
lectures.description: Explores fluid speciation and precipitation in seafloor massive sulfide, porphyry copper and epithermal ore systems.

lectures.title: What a Drill Hole Does Not Know: Exploring a Hidden Ore Body
lectures.description: Builds ore-body estimates from maps, core, surveys and assays while treating inverse problems, sampling bias, grade/tonnage and mine feasibility.

lectures.title: The Heat Is There, but Can We Reach It? Geothermal Energy Underground
lectures.description: Distinguishes heat flow, geothermal gradient, natural hydrothermal and enhanced reservoirs, electrical conversion, scaling and induced seismicity.

lectures.title: The Valley with Three Possible Futures: A Geological Field Investigation
lectures.description: Works through an explicitly fictional valley where slope, ore, geothermal and water-quality evidence support competing geological models and different tests.
